pattern.top_pattern: CA acute hospital spend is concentrated in three PPO Local providers
key_driver_codes: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
Other Disorders of Nervous System with MCC
pattern.pattern_details: In CA PPO Local acute hospitals, spend is concentrated in three providers with two distinct drivers. UCI Medical Center and Huntington Health are mainly seeing more admissions, while Hoag Hospital Newport Beach shows both more admissions and higher paid per admit. This is a targeted provider-mix issue inside one product and facility setting, not a broad statewide pricing jump.
pattern.why_it_matters: Concentrated provider patterns can usually be addressed faster with targeted UM and network action than with broad policy changes.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Run provider-specific admission source and level-of-care review for UCI Medical Center and Huntington Health, and pair that with contract and reimbursement review for Hoag Hospital Newport Beach, focusing on recurring UTI and nervous system admissions.
evidence_summary: UCI Medical Center added +$0.6M with 27 more admissions, while paid per admit fell by about $0.4K.
Huntington Health added +$0.5M with 23 more admissions and largely flat paid per admit.
Hoag Hospital Newport Beach added +$0.7M with 24 more admissions and paid per admit up about $3.6K.
UTI and nervous system DRGs were recurring drivers, each adding about +$87K to +$140K.
